Logit-scale binomial output requires interior site-year proportions.
✖ Expected `0 < C < n for every retained cell`.
ℹ Actual: `C = 0, n = 10`.
ℹ Fix: Use `vst = "arcsine"`, `vst = "none"`, or filter boundary cells before logit output.

Logit-scale binomial output requires interior site-year proportions.
✖ Expected `0 < C < n for every retained cell`.
ℹ Actual: `C = 10, n = 10`.
ℹ Fix: Use `vst = "arcsine"`, `vst = "none"`, or filter boundary cells before logit output.

Logit-scale binomial output requires interior site-year proportions.
✖ Expected `0 < C < n for every retained cell`.
ℹ Actual: `C = 0, n = 1`.
ℹ Fix: Use `vst = "arcsine"`, `vst = "none"`, or filter boundary cells before logit output.

`anscombe = TRUE` is incompatible with `binomial_bc`.
✖ Expected `bias_correction = NULL`.
ℹ Actual: `bias_correction = "binomial_bc"`.
ℹ Fix: Use the Anscombe approximation without an additional n-1 correction.

`anscombe = TRUE` is incompatible with Agresti-Coull boundary regularization.
✖ Expected `boundary_method = "wilson_floor" or "none"`.
ℹ Actual: `boundary_method = "agresti_coull"`.
ℹ Fix: Use the Anscombe transform without Agresti-Coull regularization.

Finite-population SRSWOR requires `fpc >= n` in every retained group.
✖ Expected `population_size >= sample size`.
ℹ Actual: `fpc = 7, n = 8`.
ℹ Fix: Use the fixed population size for each site-year; `fpc = n` is a valid census.

`fpc` must be NULL or positive whole-number finite-population sizes.
✖ Expected `NULL, one population size, or an input-row-aligned vector`.
ℹ Actual: `class = numeric; length = 1`.
ℹ Fix: Use a scalar whole population size or repeat a group-constant size on every input row.

Agresti-Coull boundary adjustment is not defined for Scenario C matrix output.
✖ Expected `no boundary cells, or boundary_method = "wilson_floor" / "none"`.
ℹ Actual: `a, b`.
ℹ Fix: Use `boundary_method = "wilson_floor"` for `vjt = TRUE`, or request scalar-only output.

Scenario C whole-matrix binomial correction requires n > 1.
✖ Expected `n > 1`.
ℹ Actual: `1`.
ℹ Fix: Use the plug-in matrix for a one-unit group.
